speaker: Jim Cramer
text: You have to be willing to fail. If you are not willing to fail, you are not going to succeed. The greatest investors I have ever known were not afraid of being wrong — they were afraid of not learning from being wrong.

speaker: Jim Cramer
text: Hard work beats talent when talent doesn't work hard. I have seen so many brilliant people who just couldn't get out of their own way, and I have seen so many people who weren't the smartest in the room but just outworked everyone around them.

speaker: Jim Cramer
text: The NSLS is doing something really important — it is giving students the tools and the community to actually believe in themselves. That is the foundation of everything. You cannot build a career, you cannot build a life, without first believing you are capable of it.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: There is no such thing as an overnight success. I was an overnight success after thirteen years of working in the business. I was dancing in go-go boots and doing comedy in New York for years before Laugh-In. Nothing happens overnight. It takes persistence, it takes dedication, and it takes a willingness to fail and get back up again.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: I wanted to be happy. That was my driving force. Not fame, not money — I wanted to be happy. And I think that when you follow that instinct, when you follow happiness, you end up finding your purpose. Because what makes you happy is usually what you are meant to do.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: You have to know who you are. You have to know your own value system. Because if you don't know who you are, other people will tell you who you are — and you will believe them. You will become what other people say you are, rather than what you know yourself to be.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: Don't ever apologize for your success. Don't ever apologize for working hard and achieving something. There are people who will try to make you feel guilty for succeeding, but success is not something to be ashamed of. It is something to be celebrated and shared.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: Follow your own path, not someone else's. Everybody has a different journey. Everybody has a different gift. When you try to copy someone else's path, you lose your own. The most important thing is to discover what is uniquely yours and pursue that with everything you have.

speaker: Goldie Hawn
text: I have a thirst for knowledge that has never left me. I am always curious, always wanting to learn more, always asking questions. Curiosity is one of the greatest gifts you can cultivate in yourself. It keeps you young, it keeps you engaged with life, and it opens doors that you never even knew existed.

speaker: Jamie Foxx
text: You have to have the drive, you have to have the hustle. Nobody is going to hand you anything. I grew up knowing that if I wanted something, I had to go get it. My grandmother instilled that in me — the idea that the world does not owe you anything, but if you work hard enough, you can earn everything.

speaker: Jamie Foxx
text: You have to learn how to shut out the noise. Everybody has an opinion about what you should do with your life. Everybody has something to say about your dreams. But at some point you have to get quiet, go inside yourself, and listen to what you know to be true about who you are and what you are capable of.

speaker: Jamie Foxx
text: Adversity is what builds you. Every time something hard happened in my life, every time I got knocked down, every time I failed — that was the thing that made me stronger. I would not trade any of the hard stuff because without it I would not have the resilience, the perspective, or the gratitude that I have today.

speaker: Jamie Foxx
text: Fear has nothing on the other side of it. On the other side of fear is everything you want. When I was scared to go on stage, when I was scared to take a role, when I was scared to try something new — every single time I pushed through that fear, something great was waiting for me on the other side.

speaker: Jamie Foxx
text: My grandmother never put a ceiling on what I could become. She never said that's too big a dream or that's not realistic for someone like you. She said go for it. She said be great. And that belief — having just one person in your corner who believes in you without limits — that changes everything.

speaker: Arianna Huffington
text: We are living with a burnout epidemic, and I am here to tell you that burnout is not a badge of honor. Burnout is not the price of success. The way we define success right now — money and power — is a two-legged stool. It will topple over. We need to add a third leg: well-being, wisdom, and our ability to wonder.

speaker: Arianna Huffington
text: The future is going to belong to the undistracted. The people who can focus, who can be present, who can resist the constant pull of notifications and interruptions — those are the people who are going to create the most value, make the best decisions, and lead the most fulfilling lives.

speaker: Arianna Huffington
text: Failure is not the opposite of success — it is a stepping stone to success. I have been fired, I have had books rejected, I have had major public failures. And every single one of those failures taught me something essential that I needed to know in order to eventually succeed. Failure is data.

speaker: Arianna Huffington
text: Life is a dance between making things happen and letting things happen. Sometimes you push, sometimes you yield. Sometimes you pursue relentlessly, and sometimes you have to step back and trust that things are unfolding as they should. Wisdom is knowing which moment calls for which response.

speaker: Arianna Huffington
text: Fearlessness is not the absence of fear. Fearlessness is having fears and doing it anyway. It is moving forward even when you are terrified. It is making the call, writing the book, starting the company, having the conversation — even when every cell in your body is screaming at you to play it safe.

speaker: Kelly Ripa
text: When someone tells you no, what they are really telling you is not right now, not this way, not with me. No is not a permanent condition. No is a redirect. Some of the best things that ever happened in my career came after someone told me no — because that no pushed me to find a better yes.

speaker: Kelly Ripa
text: Nobody is going to advocate for you harder than you advocate for yourself. You have to know your worth, you have to be able to articulate your worth, and you have to be willing to walk away if your worth is not recognized. Self-advocacy is not arrogance — it is self-respect.

speaker: Kelly Ripa
text: The things that scare you the most are usually the things you most need to do. Every time I have leaned into discomfort, every time I have said yes to something that terrified me, I have grown in ways I could not have anticipated. Comfort is the enemy of growth.

speaker: Kelly Ripa
text: Setting boundaries is not selfish — it is survival. You cannot pour from an empty cup. You cannot show up for others if you do not show up for yourself first. Learning to say no to the things that drain you is what allows you to say yes with full energy to the things that matter most.

speaker: Kelly Ripa
text: Watch how the people above you treat the people below them. That will tell you everything you need to know about who they are and what kind of leader they are. The person who is charming to the boss but dismissive to the assistant is not a person of character. Character is revealed in how you treat people who can do nothing for you.

speaker: Andrew Yang
text: Catalyzing real change takes years, sometimes decades. When I started the presidential campaign, people thought it was a vanity project. speaker: Andrew Yang
text: When you commit fully to something, people respond differently. There is a level of credibility and seriousness that comes only from total commitment — from burning the ships. When I left my job and went all in on the campaign, doors opened that never would have opened if I had kept one foot out.

speaker: Andrew Yang
text: My parents came to this country with almost nothing, and they had a growth mindset before anyone used that term. They believed that effort and education could transform their circumstances, and they were right. That immigrant mentality — that the rules can be bent, that your current position is not your final position — is something every American should carry.

speaker: Andrew Yang
text: You have to be willing to be humiliated for the things you believe in. I stood on a national debate stage and talked about ideas that people laughed at. I gave speeches to rooms of twelve people. There is a real cost to standing up for something before it is popular, and you have to decide if the belief is worth the cost.

speaker: Anita Hill
text: The work of equality is a relay race. The people who came before us handed us a baton, and it is our responsibility to carry it as far as we can and hand it to the next generation in a better position than we found it. None of us will see the finish line in our lifetime, but every step forward matters.

speaker: Anita Hill
text: Leadership is not just about responsibility — it is about accountability. Real leaders do not just take credit when things go well. They stand up and own it when things go wrong. They ask what could I have done differently, what do I owe to the people I lead, and how do I make it right.

speaker: Anita Hill
text: The best leaders propose solutions rather than impose them. They bring people into the process of solving problems rather than delivering answers from on high. That kind of leadership builds ownership, it builds trust, and it builds organizations that can sustain themselves beyond any single leader.

speaker: Anita Hill
text: The world is waiting for your generation. I am not saying that as a platitude — I mean it seriously. The problems we face are going to require new thinking, new courage, and new voices. Your generation is less constrained by the orthodoxies that have held previous generations back. That is not a burden; that is an extraordinary advantage.

speaker: Marc Randolph
text: Ideas do not count. Every single idea you have is probably wrong in some way. The only thing that matters is whether you are willing to go out and test your idea against reality. The companies that win are not the ones with the best ideas — they are the ones that figure out fastest which of their ideas are actually flawed.

speaker: Marc Randolph
text: Do something rather than think about doing something. The bias toward action is the single most important trait of a successful entrepreneur. You can spend years planning and perfecting and preparing, or you can get out there with something imperfect today and start learning. The learning only happens when you start.

speaker: Marc Randolph
text: You do not need the perfect idea, the perfect team, or the perfect amount of money to get started. You need to start with what you have. Netflix did not start with streaming — we started by mailing DVDs. The company you end up with is never the company you set out to build. Start with what is available to you right now.

speaker: Marc Randolph
text: Ask for what you want. This sounds simple, but most people are terrified to ask directly for the thing they need. I have seen more careers stall and more deals fall apart simply because someone could not bring themselves to ask clearly and directly for what they wanted. The worst anyone can say is no, and no is not the end of the world.

speaker: Marc Randolph
text: Leadership is situational. There is no one style that works in every context. The best leaders I have known are chameleons — they read the room, they read the people, and they adjust their approach accordingly. Sometimes you need to be directive, sometimes you need to step back, and wisdom is knowing which moment you are in.

text: Bad things happen in life. If you just sit and soak in your sadness then you're just gonna smell like that. Hurdlers in the Olympics fall and trip on hurdles, it doesn't mean that they quit the business. You have to get back up and keep jumping.

text: You work harder than everyone else and you don't complain about it. And you find joy in it. And when you find joy in the job you have, then you can close your eyes and imagine the job you want. text: The work is the thing. It's not what you get from the work, the money or the rewards or the trinkets or the things. The work itself needs to be your purpose. speaker: Rachael Ray
text: You don't work for those people. You work for yourself. If you don't believe in what you're doing, you're doing the wrong thing. Put that out there and don't pay attention too much to the negative, because you will never change the negative.

speaker: Rachael Ray
text: I think all of life is one big mistake we should all reveal to each other. There's nothing wrong with being wrong. You learn more from being wrong than from feeling that you're right. They're gonna be your biggest successes.

text: Family is what's provided all the balance and sort of my whole reason for being. speaker: Jack Black
text: When you're thinking about what direction you want your life to go in, ask what do you wanna do as opposed to what do you wanna be? Because the best thing is to think about what you wanna do. speaker: Jack Black
text: I like to feel like we're putting on a show together and that they're listening. That's where the real fun is. And when you start having fun, you feel like that's when the best work happens too.

speaker: Jack Black
text: Setting aside some time every day to just be quiet and listen to the deepest parts of yourself — I've found great benefit in that in my life and all the best inspirations and directions that I've taken have been as a result of just being quiet, and listening to what my heart has to say about any given thing that I'm working on or thinking about. You can't affect change in the world and you can't make a difference unless you're in a good place, unless you're present.

speaker: Bill Nye
text: I wanted to influence young people. I had gotten a job at Boeing, I was a young guy, and I just realized that kids are the future. I wanted to influence the future. speaker: Bill Nye
text: People don't regret what they do, they regret what they don't do. Most of the time when people look back on their lives or even look back on last summer, you regret what you didn't do more than what you did do.

speaker: Bill Nye
text: As we say in the theater, you gotta take that nervousness and turn it into excitement. What's possible is often a little more than you think at first.

speaker: Bill Nye
text: There is no big break. They're just breaks. They're just bricks on the ziggurat, the stepped pyramid. So you have regrets about a couple of bricks, but overall, the pyramid is getting bigger. It's always a compromise on jobs you're not sure about. Balance.

speaker: Tanya Acker
text: The law is really the study, not just of how to try a case in a courtroom. I wanted to be able to make a living and I also wanted to have the power to use the tools that I've got to change the things that I think need to be changed.

speaker: Tanya Acker
text: You should jump at opportunities. You should look to try to pursue things that excite you. Do them well and realize that sometimes you don't know what's next. You do something well that's right in front of you and it could lead to something entirely different. As you're exploring, take on your tasks and do them well, do them with pride, with the expectation that that job well done will very well lead to something else that you don't even know about.

speaker: Tanya Acker
text: Success is the best revenge. The best thing that you can do when someone is trying to diminish you or belittle you or tear you down or disrespect you for any reason, it's for you to remind yourself who you are. That person doesn't define you. You are the definer of you. And anyone who would tell you otherwise for whatever reason, that's a voice that you should use to propel you to success.

speaker: Tanya Acker
text: We all sort of have responsibilities. We're here because some people mentored us and it's our responsibility to pay it forward. It is something that we all need to model and provide to others. We gotta pay it forward.

speaker: Tanya Acker
text: Any time I've been tested or challenged or disappointed by something, it really has been an opportunity for me to think about what I'm after. The best thing that you can do is to use a challenge as the best way to propel you to think about how you're gonna do things differently. How are you going to make sure that the next time something like this happens you're better prepared not just to meet it, but to not let it break your spirit.

speaker: Valerie Jarrett
text: Take time to build friendships and relationships because these folks will be with you throughout your life. When you walk into a meeting or a classroom and you've had dinner with somebody the night before and they're at the table, it gives you so much more confidence to speak up. It's who you know and do they know you.

speaker: Valerie Jarrett
text: The failures have taught me so much and if nothing else they've taught me that I'm resilient. And that I can get back up and I think that's the advantage of age. The question is really not is every chapter perfect, but do the chapters add up to a whole life. Did you love, were you loved? Did you feel as though, the short time that we have on this earth, that you made a difference in somebody else's life.

speaker: Valerie Jarrett
text: Leadership is about motivating people to move in a direction where they might not have gone but for your leadership. They have to know that you are authentic because you're asking them to do something different than what they're already doing, and they're not gonna do that if they don't trust you.

speaker: Valerie Jarrett
text: Integrity — you have nothing more important than your reputation. Have core values. My dad used to tell me when I was very young, color well within the lines, and if you color well within the lines then you'll always be safe.

speaker: Valerie Jarrett
text: The advantage of having a good education is it gives you a safety net where you can take some chances. speaker: Tiki Barber
text: Every relationship you make will be valuable and you never know when those opportunities that seem imperfect are actually the perfect one. speaker: Tiki Barber
text: When opportunity comes your way, whether it's the perfect opportunity or an imperfect one, you have to be ready. speaker: Tiki Barber
text: Opportunities often do come from failures. My manager said to me, look, you gotta divorce yourself from football because you might not make it. He was being real with me. These opportunities, sometimes they're not perfect all the time, but you gotta be ready for them.

speaker: Tiki Barber
text: Sometimes you have to create your own opportunities. I went through what I now know was a depression, but I realized that if I wanted to get out of it, I had to create my own opportunity. So I got up and started working out again. I recreated this energy, this vigor inside of myself and it started opening up opportunities again because of relationships that I had. When failure comes about as it undoubtedly will, you have to sometimes recreate yourself.

speaker: Tiki Barber
text: When you think about the life and the path that you're going to take, whether it's succinct and you're straight in line, don't forget that you might fall off for a variety of reasons — one, cause you find a better opportunity, two, you might fail out of it. But ultimately, when failure comes about as it undoubtedly will, you have to sometimes recreate yourself.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: When the student is ready the teacher will appear. I always had mentors, I always did. I was always looking up to people and you always have that when you're coming up cause there's always somebody that you wanna be like, you know, I want that.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: You must learn the business. And it's very helpful to have a job where you're working for someone, you're working for a company that you'd like to do it yourself so if you could get one or two or three years in that job to see how it's supposed to be done before you go into business, that is very helpful.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: I think you must acknowledge whatever role you had in your downfall or your adversity. I think if you can acknowledge that, then you can go forward. If you're just wandering around saying everything, nothing's my fault, you know, they did this to me — then that's gonna be tough. You have to own your part.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: Intelligence is the ability to adapt. You can say, I've changed my mind. People, many people that I work with are very reluctant to say that. They think it's a form of weakness to say, you know, I thought that, I changed my mind. I think that's a sign of strength, changing your mind.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: I always say don't quit before the miracle. And I think anything that keeps you interacting with your fellow human beings in this day and age is a good thing. Exchanging ideas with your peers is a big advantage in a real learning environment.

speaker: Steve Madden
text: To really be successful you have to be able to trust people. If you can find yourself in that position where you disagree with someone but you trust them and you think they're smart enough that you go, okay I disagree with them, but they're so smart, I'm gonna go with them on this — that's real. If you can get that, you're really in good shape.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: Oftentimes in life we spend so much time being afraid of what won't happen, that we never try and pursue the idea of what will happen. Don't use the lottery logic to stop yourself, use it to start. Play and go, what if I do win? Think of all the amazing things that can happen to you if you do.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: I think one of the toughest things a leader must possess, and it's often overlooked, is the ability to see when and if you are wrong. The ability to change longstanding beliefs that you may possess. Because it's hard enough as a person to change their minds. It's twice as hard to change your mind when you don't have to because you're in power.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: Humor became your currency. Humor became your coping mechanism. One thing my family always had was laughter. Through the toughest times, through the hungriest days, we found a way to laugh. We didn't laugh because the situation wasn't important to us. We laughed because that's how we dealt with how important it was.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: You always have the power to determine yourself, how you see yourself, and how you wish for yourself to be seen. You cannot control how somebody views you, but you can choose how you see yourself and how you wish to be seen. The way you react to that world is what you have the most control over.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: We are taught from the very beginning to aspire to other people's dreams and goals. And sometimes we don't just take a step back and go, why? Why do you want to be a lawyer? Why do you want to be a doctor? If you're going to work your whole life, then why not enjoy it? You should be enjoying yourself.

speaker: Trevor Noah
text: Give yourself a schedule, give yourself a routine. Give yourself goals that are achievable, that are still a challenge that you seek to improve on, but things that make you feel better about yourself and things that can help you get where you're going. As humans, we overestimate what we can do or learn in a year, and we underestimate what we can achieve in a decade.

text: If you don't get into a play or a movie that I wanted to get into, I just feel like, in some way, it was not meant to happen. text: I've seen really talented people who don't have the motivation or discipline fall off. Passion with no talent usually leads to kind of good things. Talent with no passion is really hard. text: When I was not getting acting jobs, I would write a play. And the backup plan actually helped the front plan. text: I believe that the power of that insult was half responsible for the success I would have over the next 20 years, because whenever I was out of ideas, whenever I was in the hock, whenever I owed the bank money, when everything was going wrong, I would think of those words, 'You'll never succeed without me,' and I would think of one more idea. speaker: Barbara Corcoran
text: I found the only difference between the phenomenal people and everybody else was when they took a hit, they didn't feel sorry for themselves. They took hits like everybody else, in fact more so because they push so much harder. But they were wired in a way that lacked the gene that felt sorry for themselves.

speaker: Barbara Corcoran
text: Fun is the most underutilized card in business today. If you could develop a fun environment where you work, everybody does better work. text: I think trust is undervalued. The ability to make people trust you is essential if you want to build a business. speaker: Barbara Corcoran

speaker: Malcolm Gladwell

speaker: Malcolm Gladwell

speaker: Malcolm Gladwell

text: The whole point about building genuine relationships is you don't go in it for the 'what's in it for me.' You go in it and you have a relationship and you help people, and then when you do that, more often than not down the line, it comes back to benefit you somehow.

speaker: Emily Balcetis
text: We can be miscalibrated about what we think we can accomplish, or we set our sights too high, especially at the beginning, and we fizzle out too soon. speaker: Emily Balcetis
text: When we're dreaming big and we set that very lofty, long-term goal, we need to start thinking concretely about the actions that we can take today, this week, this month that's going to help us in that right direction. The other thing that we need to do is start thinking about the obstacles that we're going to encounter along the way — foreshadowing failure is actually setting up a plan B, a plan C, a safety net.

text: Narrowly focusing your attention, imagining that there's a spotlight just on this target that you've chosen, induces this illusion that it's closer. speaker: Emily Balcetis
text: Rather than thinking like, 'I messed up, I'm off course, I lost my streak,' we don't have to think about it that way. We can try to find fresh starts. text: Diversity is what is at the heart of what innovation really is. Innovation is creating new things, giving new ideas life. How do we innovate? We get new perspectives. We get different ideas. text: Too often, we treat education, and knowledge, and wisdom, and research as abstract concepts. We don't put it into practice. Life's big challenges are very practical.
